mainTopic: Which invalid bird offerings count as נבלה after מליקה, and the dispute between רב and רבי יוחנן over a זר's מליקה
overview: The משנה finishes its list of bird offerings that still count as נבלה after מליקה, so they make a person impure when swallowed. Its rule is this: a bird that became invalid during the holy service is not נבלה, but a bird that was unfit before the service is. In the גמרא, רב rules that pinching with the left hand or at night does not make the bird נבלה, but pinching by a זר or with a knife does. The גמרא asks why a זר is different, since a זר may do שחיטה. It answers that שחיטה is not a true עבודה. This answer is defended twice. First, the פרה אדומה needs a כהן, just as checking נגעים does, without its שחיטה being an עבודה. Second, we do not learn בית המקדש rules from a במה. רבי יוחנן then disagrees with רב: a זר's מליקה does not make the bird נבלה, though a knife does. The גמרא challenges רב from the word ״כל״ in the משנה and answers that the משנה states a rule and then explains it. A second ״כל״ challenge from the משנה's summary rule is answered on the next amud.

steps.title: Birds that were never fit still make impure
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists birds that were unfit before the service even began. Pinching their necks does not stop them from being נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Turtledoves that are too young, young pigeons that are too old, or a bird with a dried-up wing, a blinded eye, or a cut-off leg: even after pinching, it makes a person impure when it is in his throat.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list of cases where a pinched bird still counts as נבלה. All these birds were unfit from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pinching (מליקה) normally counts as a kosher way to kill a bird offering, so the bird is not נבלה. But these birds were never fit to be offered at all, so their pinching counts for nothing. The result: the bird is plain נבלה, and נבלת עוף טהור makes a person impure when he swallows it.

keyTerms.meaning: Turtledoves; only adult ones may be offered
Young pigeons; only young ones may be offered
Pinching the back of a bird offering's neck with the fingernail
The throat; a kosher bird's נבלה makes a person impure while he swallows it
Makes impure

phrases.english: Turtledoves whose time has not arrived,
and young pigeons whose time has passed;
one whose wing dried up,
one whose eye was blinded,
or one whose leg was cut off –
it makes a person impure in the throat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of cases from the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Birds that were unfit before the service began are still נבלה after מליקה and make a person impure in the throat.

steps.title: The משנה's general rule
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sums up its cases: a flaw that happened in the holy service does not make impure, but a flaw from before does.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the rule: anything whose flaw happened in the holy service does not make impure in the throat. If its flaw did not happen in the holy service, it does make impure in the throat.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives one rule that explains its whole list of cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the bird was a proper offering and only became invalid through a mistake during the service, the pinching still works enough to keep it from being נבלה. If the bird was never fit for the holy service, the pinching does not help, so it stays נבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the general rule
Its flaw happened within the holy service

steps.whatToRemember: Flaw inside the service: not נבלה, no impurity. Flaw from before the service: נבלה, makes impure in the throat.
steps.confusionAlert: Both kinds of bird are invalid as offerings. The rule only decides whether the bird also counts as נבלה for טומאה.

phrases.english: This is the rule:
anything whose flaw happened in the holy –
phrases.notes: He means a bird that was fit, and only became invalid during the service itself.

phrases.english: does not make a person impure in the throat;
if its flaw did not happen in the holy –
it makes a person impure in the throat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the list of cases into one principle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A flaw inside the holy service does not make the bird נבלה; a flaw from before the service does.

steps.title: רב sorts four flawed pinchings
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that pinching with the left hand or at night does not make the bird נבלה, but pinching by a זר or with a knife does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: pinching with the left hand or at night does not make impure in the throat. Pinching by a זר or with a knife does make impure in the throat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ruling from רב that puts four invalid pinchings into two groups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All four pinchings are invalid for the offering. רב says that left hand and night still count as "flaws in the holy service," so the bird is not נבלה. A זר and a knife are treated as if no real מליקה happened, so the bird is נבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: The left hand
Night
A non-כהן
A knife (instead of the fingernail)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the question in the next step: what makes some invalid pinchings different from others?

phrases.english: Gemara: Rav said:
The left hand and night –
phrases.notes: He means pinching done with the left hand, or done at night.

phrases.english: do not make a person impure in the throat,
a non-kohen and a knife –
do make a person impure in the throat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the משנה's rule to four specific flawed pinchings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Left hand and night: not נבלה. זר and knife: נבלה.

steps.title: Why is a non-kohen different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why left hand and night are treated well, and then shows that a זר seems to fit the same reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is the left hand different? Because it is valid somewhere, on יום הכפורים. And night is valid somewhere, for burning אברים and פדרים. But a זר is also valid somewhere, in שחיטה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason for רב's ruling about left hand and night, and then challenges his ruling about a זר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is: if an action is valid in at least one Temple service, a flawed pinching of that kind still counts as "inside the holy." The left hand is valid on יום הכפורים, and night is valid for burning אברים and פדרים. But a זר may do שחיטה, so a זר's pinching should also not make the bird נבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different?
A case where it is valid
Limbs and fats of offerings burned on the מזבח
Slaughtering an animal

phrases.english: Why is the left hand different?
Because it has a case where it is valid, on Yom Kippur,
phrases.notes: On יום הכפורים the כהן גדול carries the spoon of incense into the קודש הקדשים in his left hand.

phrases.english: and night – it has a case where it is valid,
with limbs and fats;
phrases.notes: These may be burned on the מזבח all night long.

phrases.english: a non-kohen also –
has a case where he is valid, in slaughtering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling about a זר using the same reasoning that explains left hand and night.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that pinching by a זר makes the bird נבלה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If being valid in some Temple service is enough for left hand and night, a זר should also qualify, since a זר may do שחיטה.

steps.title: Slaughtering is not a real Temple service
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שחיטה is not counted as a true עבודה, so it cannot help a זר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Slaughtering is not a Temple service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב: a זר's being allowed to slaughter does not count, because slaughtering is not a true service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The left hand and night are valid in real Temple services. A זר is only allowed to do שחיטה, which is not counted as a real עבודה. So a זר has no valid case in any real service, and his pinching leaves the bird נבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: A real Temple service
Not

steps.whatToRemember: Left hand and night are valid in some real עבודה, so their pinching is not נבלה. A זר is valid only in שחיטה, which is not a real עבודה, so his pinching is נבלה.

phrases.english: Slaughtering is not a Temple service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רב's ruling about a זר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: שחיטה is not a true עבודה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A זר is valid for שחיטה, so his pinching should not make the bird נבלה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only being valid in a true עבודה counts. Since שחיטה is not a true עבודה, a זר's pinching leaves the bird נבלה.

steps.title: Challenge from the red heifer slaughtered by a non-priest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that שחיטה is not a true עבודה. רבי זירא rules that a פרה אדומה slaughtered by a זר is פסולה, and רב shows the source in the פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is שחיטה really not an עבודה? But רבי זירא said that if a זר slaughters the פרה אדומה, it is פסולה. And רב pointed to the source: the תורה mentions אלעזר, and it calls the פרה a 'חוקה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave in step 5. If a זר is not allowed to slaughter the פרה אדומה, it looks like שחיטה is a real עבודה after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said a זר may slaughter because שחיטה is not a true עבודה. Here we have a שחיטה that a זר is not allowed to do. That suggests שחיטה does count as a כהן's job, so the answer to the זר problem seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: The red heifer (פרה אדומה), whose ashes are used to purify people from טומאת מת
A non-כהן
'Statute'. In this teaching it shows that the details mentioned in the פרשה are required
אלעזר הכהן, who handled the first פרה אדומה
Pointed to or showed a source

phrases.english: And is it not [a true service]?!
phrases.notes: This goes back to step 5, which said שחיטה is not a true עבודה.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Zeira say:
the slaughter of the red heifer by a non-priest is invalid;
and Rav pointed out [the source] for it:
Elazar, and 'statute'!
phrases.notes: במדבר 19:3 names אלעזר, and במדבר 19:2 calls it a 'חוקה'. Together they show that a כהן must do it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the תירוץ of step 5, which said שחיטה is not a true עבודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שחיטה is not a real עבודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: פרה אדומה slaughtered by a זר is פסולה, so שחיטה seems to need a כהן and seems to count as an עבודה.

steps.title: The red heifer is a different kind of holy item
steps.stepSummary: The פרה אדומה is different because it is קדשי בדק הבית, not an altar offering. So its rules cannot teach us about normal קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פרה is different, because it has the status of קדשי בדק הבית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the פרה אדומה is a separate category, so it cannot be compared to a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פרה is not brought on the מזבח. It counts as an item made holy for the בית המקדש's upkeep. So whatever is special about its שחיטה tells us nothing about the שחיטה of altar offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different
Items made holy for the upkeep of the בית המקדש, not for the מזבח

phrases.english: The heifer is different,
for it is [in the category of] items consecrated for Temple maintenance.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction (the case belongs to a different category)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פרה proves that every שחיטה is an עבודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פרה is קדשי בדק הבית, so it is no proof for קדשי מזבח.

steps.title: Shouldn't altar offerings need a priest even more?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back with a קל וחומר. If even קדשי בדק הבית, which are less holy, need כהונה for their שחיטה, then קדשי מזבח should certainly need it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it all the more so? If קדשי בדק הבית need a כהן, do we even need to say that קדשי מזבח do?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the distinction of step 7. It argues that the difference makes the challenge stronger, not weaker.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קדשי מזבח are holier than קדשי בדק הבית. So if the less holy פרה needs a כהן to slaughter it, a קרבן should need one even more. That would make שחיטה an עבודה again.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so (a קל וחומר)
Items made holy for the מזבח, meaning the קרבנות
Priesthood; here, needing a כהן to do the act
Is it even needed [to say]? This means 'obviously so'

phrases.english: But is it not all the more so:
if items consecrated for Temple maintenance require the priesthood,
is it necessary to say so about items consecrated for the altar?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the distinction in step 7 by turning it into a קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that פרה is different because it is קדשי בדק הבית.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: the less holy category needs a כהן, so the holier category should need one too. That would make שחיטה an עבודה.

steps.title: Needing a priest does not make it a service, like checking נגעים
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי explains that the פרה's שחיטה needs a כהן even though it is not an עבודה. It is just like a כהן checking מראות נגעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי said: It is just like looking at the shades of נגעים. That is not an עבודה, and still it needs a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שישא answers the קל וחומר. A כהן is needed for the פרה, but that does not make its שחיטה an עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר assumed that 'needs a כהן' means 'is an עבודה.' רב שישא shows these are separate: looking at נגעים needs a כהן, yet it is not an עבודה at all. So the פרה teaches nothing about whether שחיטה of קדשי מזבח is an עבודה, and the answer of step 5 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is just like, the same as
The shades of צרעת marks, which a כהן must look at and rule on
A real service in the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: Needing a כהן does not mean something is an עבודה. The פרה's שחיטה needs a כהן, like checking נגעים, yet it is not an עבודה. So the rule that a זר may slaughter קרבנות stands.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up 'only a כהן may do it' with 'it is an עבודה.' The קל וחומר in step 8 worked only because it treated these as the same, and רב שישא shows they are not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This defends the answer of step 5, that שחיטה is not a true עבודה. That answer explains why a זר's pinching of the bird is treated differently from pinching with the left hand or at night.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha, son of Rav Idi, said:
It is just like the shades of leprous marks,
which is not a service,
and yet requires the priesthood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי: מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַמַּרְאוֹת נְגָעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קל וחומר of step 8 by showing that needing a כהן is separate from being an עבודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison to a parallel case (מידי דהוה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the פרה needs a כהן, its שחיטה must be an עבודה, and altar offerings should need a כהן even more.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פרה needs a כהן without its שחיטה being an עבודה, like נגעים. So no קל וחומר can be built for קדשי מזבח.

steps.title: Why not learn from a private altar?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests learning from a במה, where a זר was allowed to offer, that a זר's מליקה can be valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us learn from a private altar!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why a bird pinched by a זר becomes a נבלה. At a במה, a זר was allowed to do the service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a private במה, the service did not need a כהן. So there is at least one setting where a זר's מליקה works. The גמרא suggests using that setting as a model for the בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: A private altar. It was allowed at certain times before the בית המקדש was built.
And let us learn (derive)
A non-כהן
Pinching the neck of a bird קרבן

phrases.english: But let us derive it from a private altar!
phrases.notes: He means: at a במה a זר could offer, so a זר's מליקה should not ruin the bird here either.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a new source showing that a זר's service could be valid.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a bird pinched by a זר is a נבלה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: At a במה a זר's service is valid. So זר service is not inherently invalid, and we could learn from there.

steps.title: We do not learn from a private altar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the rules of the בית המקדש cannot be learned from a במה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not derive anything from a private altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. A במה is a different, lower kind of setting, so its rules do not carry over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fact that a זר could offer at a במה only shows how the במה worked. It says nothing about the stricter rules of the בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not derive (learn)

phrases.english: One does not derive from a private altar.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the proposed source as invalid for this kind of learning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rules of a במה could teach us about the בית המקדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: A במה is not used as a source for the rules of the בית המקדש.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to learn from a private altar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim from step 11. A ברייתא learns from a במה that a יוצא which went up on the מזבח does not come down.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we don't? But a ברייתא teaches: From where do we know that a יוצא, if it went up on the altar, does not come down? Because a יוצא is valid on a private altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that seems to do exactly what step 11 said we cannot do. It learns a בית המקדש rule from a במה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יוצא is a קרבן part that left the עזרה. That makes it unfit, yet if it was already placed on the מזבח it stays there. The ברייתא's reason is that a יוצא is fine at a במה, which seems to show that we do learn from a במה.

keyTerms.meaning: A קרבן (or its parts) that went out of the עזרה and became unfit
If it went up on the מזבח, it does not come down

steps.confusionAlert: ״עלה לא ירד״ does not mean the יוצא was valid from the start. It is an unfit item, and the rule only says that once it is on the מזבח, we leave it there.

phrases.english: And do we not? But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לַיּוֹצֵא שֶׁאִם עָלָה לֹא יֵרֵד –
phrases.english: From where do we know that an item that went out, if it went up on the altar, does not come down?
phrases.notes: "Went out" means it left the עזרה, which normally makes it unfit.

phrases.english: For an item that went out is valid on a private altar.

steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that we do not learn from a במה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא learns a rule about the מזבח in the בית המקדש from the law of a במה.

steps.title: The real source is the פסוק ״זאת תורת העולה״
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's true source is the פסוק ״זאת תורת העולה״. The במה is just extra support.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא relies on the פסוק "This is the law of the burnt offering."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא did not truly learn from the במה. Its real source is a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״זאת תורת העולה״ teaches that whatever went up on the מזבח stays there. The במה was only mentioned as backup. So the rule from step 11 still stands: we do not learn from a במה, and for רב a זר's מליקה still leaves the bird a נבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: The teacher of the ברייתא
He relies on it (as his real source)
"This is the law of the burnt offering": the source that what went up on the מזבח does not come down

steps.whatToRemember: We do not learn the rules of the בית המקדש from a במה. When a ברייתא mentions a במה, the real source is a פסוק and the במה is only support.

phrases.english: The תנא, on "This is the law of the burnt offering"
relies.
phrases.notes: The במה was only extra support. The פסוק is what really teaches the rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא אַזֹּאת תּוֹרַת הָעוֹלָה סְמִיךְ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 12 and keeps the rule of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the source. The פסוק is the real basis, and the במה is only support.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא actually derived its rule from the במה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא relies on ״זאת תורת העולה״, so we still do not learn from a במה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: a זר's מליקה does not make the bird impure, but a knife does
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees with רב. A זר's מליקה does not make the bird a נבלה. Cutting with a knife does.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי יוחנן said: If a זר did the מליקה, the bird does not make a person impure in the throat. If the bird was cut with a knife, it does make a person impure in the throat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי יוחנן's opinion, which argues with רב. For רבי יוחנן, a זר's מליקה does not turn the bird into a נבלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said a זר's מליקה makes the bird a נבלה, so it brings טומאת בית הבליעה. רבי יוחנן disagrees only about a זר: the מליקה is invalid, but the bird is not a נבלה. Both agree that cutting with a knife leaves the bird a נבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-כהן
Makes something impure
The throat. A נבלה of a kosher bird makes a person impure only when he swallows it.
A knife (instead of the כהן's fingernail)

steps.confusionAlert: Here, "מטמא אבית הבליעה" is a sign that the bird counts as a נבלה. When the text says the bird is "not מטמא," it does not mean the קרבן is kosher. It only means the bird is not a נבלה.

phrases.english: But Rabbi Yochanan says:
a non-priest's pinching does not make one impure in the throat;
a knife does make one impure in the throat.
phrases.notes: He means the bird was cut at the back of the neck with a knife instead of being pinched with the fingernail.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the opposing view to רב's opinion, which was discussed before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זר's מליקה does not make the bird a נבלה. מליקה with a knife does.

steps.title: The משנה's word ״כל״ fits רבי יוחנן but not רב
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says ״כל הפסולין שמלקו״ (all disqualified people who did מליקה). For רבי יוחנן, ״כל״ includes a זר. For רב, what does it include?
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: All disqualified people who did מליקה, their מליקה is invalid. This works well for רבי יוחנן, since ״כל״ comes to include a זר. But for רב, what does ״כל״ come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה and challenges רב from the extra word ״כל״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's rule is that these people's מליקה is invalid, but the bird is not a נבלה. For רבי יוחנן, ״כל״ adds a זר to this list. רב cannot include a זר, because for him a זר's bird is a נבלה. So the word ״כל״ seems to have no job.

keyTerms.meaning: People unfit to do the עבודה
Killing a bird קרבן by pinching the back of its neck with the fingernail
It works well for...
To include

phrases.english: We learned in the mishna:
all the disqualified people who pinched,
their pinching is invalid.
phrases.notes: The משנה means it is invalid as a קרבן, but the bird still does not become a נבלה.

phrases.english: It works well according to Rabbi Yochanan:
"All" comes to include a non-priest.
But according to Rav,
what does "all" come to include?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן ״כֹּל״ לְאֵיתוֹיֵי זָר אֶלָּא לְרַב ״כׇּל״ לְאֵיתוֹיֵי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה to support רבי יוחנן and attack רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that a זר's מליקה makes the bird a נבלה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רב, the word ״כל״ cannot include a זר, so it seems to have no purpose.

steps.title: For רב, ״כל״ includes left hand and night
steps.stepSummary: Answer for רב: ״כל״ includes מליקה done with the left hand or at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include מליקה done with the left hand and מליקה done at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רב a job for the word ״כל״ that does not involve a זר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Left-hand מליקה and nighttime מליקה are also invalid, and the bird is still not a נבלה. So ״כל״ could be adding these cases instead of a זר.

keyTerms.meaning: The left hand
Night (עבודה done at night is invalid)

phrases.english: To include the left hand and night.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets, "isn't it," and some leave it out. Either way, this is the answer.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the extra word a different purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״כל״ must include a זר, which goes against רב.

steps.title: Left hand and night are already stated openly
steps.stepSummary: The משנה already names left hand and night outright, so ״כל״ is not needed for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But left hand and night are taught openly in the משנה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the answer, because the משנה lists these cases itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An extra word should teach something that is not already written. Since the משנה names left hand and night outright, ״כל״ cannot be the source for them. So the question of what ״כל״ adds for רב comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: Openly, outright
It teaches

phrases.english: The left hand and night
are taught explicitly!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that ״כל״ includes left hand and night
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה already lists these cases, so ״כל״ would add nothing.

steps.title: The משנה gives a general rule and then explains it
steps.stepSummary: For רב, ״כל״ does not add a new case. The משנה states a general rule and then spells out the cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה teaches a general rule and then explains it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רב a new answer: ״כל״ is part of a general opening statement, not a word that adds an extra case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sometimes a משנה starts with a broad rule (״כל הפסולין״) and then lists the examples. In that case, ״כל״ is not extra and does not have to include anything new. So it does not have to include a זר, and רב's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches a general rule and then explains it in detail

phrases.english: It teaches and then explains.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 by changing how the word ״כל״ is read.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads ״כל״ as a general heading rather than a word that adds a case
steps.terutzMaskana: ״כל״ opens a general rule that the משנה then explains, so it adds nothing new.

steps.title: A second challenge to רב from the משנה's summary rule
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's summary rule, ״כל שהיה פסולו בקודש״, also says ״כל״. For רבי יוחנן it includes a זר. For רב, what does it include?
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: This is the rule: any bird whose disqualification happened in the holy place does not make garments impure in the throat. This works well for רבי יוחנן, since ״כל״ includes a זר. But for רב, what does it include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge to רב from the משנה's closing rule. Again it asks what ״כל״ adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of question as step 15, now aimed at the ״כל״ in the משנה's summary rule, ״זה הכלל״. For רבי יוחנן, ״כל״ includes a זר, whose bird is not a נבלה. For רב, a זר's bird is a נבלה, so the גמרא asks what this ״כל״ adds. The answer comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the general rule
Its disqualification happened in the holy place, during the עבודה
Clothes. A person who becomes impure from swallowing a נבלה also makes the clothes he is wearing impure.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
This is the rule:
anything whose disqualification was in the sacred place
does not make garments impure when in the throat.
It works well according to Rabbi Yochanan:
"Any" comes to include a non-priest.
But according to Rav, what does it come to include?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new challenge to רב from a later line in the same משנה, after the first challenge was answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that a זר's מליקה makes the bird a נבלה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ״כל״ in the summary rule should include something. Only רבי יוחנן has a clear case for it to include, a זר.
